   378→    def verify_python(self, app: AppConfig):
   379→        """Verify that the version of Python being used to build the app in Docker is
   380→        compatible with the version being used to run Briefcase.
   381→
   382→        Will raise an exception if the Python version is fundamentally
   383→        incompatible (i.e., if Briefcase doesn't support it); any other version
   384→        discrepancy will log a warning, but continue.
   385→
   386→        Requires that the app tools have been verified.
   387→
   388→        As a side effect of verifying Python, the `python_version_tag` will be
   389→        updated to reflect the *actual* python version, not just a generic "3".
   390→
   391→        :param app: The application being built
   392→        """
   393→        output = self.tools[app].app_context.check_output(
   394→            [
   395→                f"python{app.python_version_tag}",
   396→                "-c",
   397→                (
   398→                    "import sys; "
   399→                    "print(f'{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}')"
   400→                ),
   401→            ]
   402→        )
   403→        # Update the python version tag with the *actual* python version.
   404→        app.python_version_tag = output.split("\n")[0]
   405→        target_python_version = tuple(int(v) for v in app.python_version_tag.split("."))
   406→
   407→        if target_python_version < self.briefcase_required_python_version:
   408→            briefcase_min_version = ".".join(
   409→                str(v) for v in self.briefcase_required_python_version
   410→            )
   411→            raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   412→                f"The system python3 version provided by {app.target_image} "
   413→                f"is {app.python_version_tag}; Briefcase requires a "
   414→                f"minimum Python3 version of {briefcase_min_version}."
   415→            )
   416→        elif target_python_version != (
   417→            self.tools.sys.version_info.major,
   418→            self.tools.sys.version_info.minor,
   419→        ):
   420→            self.logger.warning(
   421→                f"""
   422→*************************************************************************
   423→** WARNING: Python version mismatch!                                   **
   424→*************************************************************************
   425→
   426→    The system python3 provided by {app.target_image} is {app.python_version_tag}.
   427→    This is not the same as your local system ({self.python_version_tag}).
   428→
   429→    Ensure you have tested for Python version compatibility before
   430→    releasing this app.
   431→
   432→*************************************************************************
   433→"""
   434→            )

   436→    def verify_system_python(self):

   438→        python.
   439→
   440→        Will raise an exception if the system Python isn't an obvious Python3, or the
   441→        Briefcase Python isn't the same version as the system Python.

   456→    def _system_requirement_tools(self, app: AppConfig):
   457→        """Utility method returning the packages and tools needed to verify system
   458→        requirements.
   459→
   460→        :param app: The app being built.
   461→        :returns: A triple containing (0) The list of package names that must
   462→            be installed at a bare minimum; (1) the arguments for the command
   463→            used to verify the existence of a package on a system, and (2)
   464→            the command used to install packages. All three values are `None`
   465→            if the system cannot be identified.
   466→        """
   467→        if app.target_vendor_base == DEBIAN:
   468→            base_system_packages = ["python3-dev", "build-essential"]
   469→            system_verify = ["dpkg", "-s"]
   470→            system_installer = ["apt", "install"]
   471→        elif app.target_vendor_base == RHEL:
   472→            base_system_packages = [
   473→                "python3-devel",
   474→                "gcc",
   475→                "make",
   476→                "pkgconf-pkg-config",
   477→            ]
   478→            system_verify = ["rpm", "-q"]
   479→            system_installer = ["dnf", "install"]
   480→        elif app.target_vendor_base == SUSE:
   481→            base_system_packages = [
   482→                "python3-devel",
   483→                "patterns-devel-base-devel_basis",
   484→            ]
   485→            system_verify = ["rpm", "-q", "--whatprovides"]
   486→            system_installer = ["zypper", "install"]
   487→        elif app.target_vendor_base == ARCH:
   488→            base_system_packages = [
   489→                "python3",
   490→                "base-devel",
   491→            ]
   492→            system_verify = ["pacman", "-Q"]
   493→            system_installer = ["pacman", "-Syu"]
   494→        else:
   495→            base_system_packages = None
   496→            system_verify = None
   497→            system_installer = None
   498→
   499→        return (
   500→            base_system_packages,
   501→            system_verify,
   502→            system_installer,

   505→    def verify_system_packages(self, app: AppConfig):
   506→        """Verify that the required system packages are installed.
   507→
   508→        :param app: The app being built.
   509→        """
   510→        (
   511→            base_system_packages,
   512→            system_verify,
   513→            system_installer,
   514→        ) = self._system_requirement_tools(app)
   515→
   516→        if system_verify is None:
   517→            self.logger.warning(
   518→                """
   519→*************************************************************************
   520→** WARNING: Can't verify system packages                               **
   521→*************************************************************************
   522→
   523→    Briefcase doesn't know how to verify the installation of system
   524→    packages on your Linux distribution. If you have any problems
   525→    building this app, ensure that the packages listed in the app's
   526→    `system_requires` setting have been installed.
   527→
   528→*************************************************************************
   529→"""
   530→            )
   531→            return
   532→
   533→        # Run a check for each package listed in the app's system_requires,
   534→        # plus the baseline system packages that are required.
   535→        missing = []
   536→        for package in base_system_packages + getattr(app, "system_requires", []):
   537→            try:
   538→                self.tools.subprocess.check_output(system_verify + [package])
   539→            except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
   540→                missing.append(package)
   541→
   542→        # If any required packages are missing, raise an error.
   543→        if missing:
   544→            raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   545→                f"""\
   546→Unable to build {app.app_name} due to missing system dependencies. Run:
   547→
   548→    sudo {' '.join(system_installer)} {' '.join(missing)}
   549→
   550→to install the missing dependencies, and re-run Briefcase.
   551→"""
   552→            )

   554→    def verify_app_tools(self, app: AppConfig):
   555→        """Verify App environment is prepared and available.
   556→
   557→        When Docker is used, create or update a Docker image for the App. Without
   558→        Docker, the host machine will be used as the App environment.
   559→
   560→        :param app: The application being built
   561→        """
   562→        # Verifying the App context is idempotent; but we have some
   563→        # additional logic that we only want to run the first time through.
   564→        # Check (and store) the pre-verify app tool state.
   565→        verify_python = not hasattr(self.tools[app], "app_context")
   566→
   567→        if self.use_docker:
   568→            DockerAppContext.verify(
   569→                tools=self.tools,
   570→                app=app,
   571→                image_tag=self.docker_image_tag(app),
   572→                dockerfile_path=self.bundle_path(app) / "Dockerfile",
   573→                app_base_path=self.base_path,
   574→                host_bundle_path=self.bundle_path(app),
   575→                host_data_path=self.data_path,
   576→                python_version=app.python_version_tag,
   577→            )
   578→
   579→            # Check the system Python on the target system to see if it is
   580→            # compatible with Briefcase.
   581→            if verify_python:
   582→                self.verify_python(app)
   583→        else:
   584→            NativeAppContext.verify(tools=self.tools, app=app)
   585→
   586→            # Check the system Python on the target system to see if it is
   587→            # compatible with Briefcase, and that the required system packages
   588→            # are installed.
   589→            if verify_python:
   590→                self.verify_system_python()
   591→                self.verify_system_packages(app)
   592→
   593→        # Establish Docker as app context before letting super set subprocess
